newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia to cut taxes that experts say too little.
newsitem.headline: Serbia to cut taxes that experts say too little.

text.p: The Serbian government pledged tax cuts, but experts said on Friday the announced fiscal adjustment was not enough to relieve the country's cash-starved economy.
Serbia's prime minister Mirko Marjanovic earlier said the government intended to cut the wages-tax ratio from 1-1.2 to 1-1. Under Serbian law, employers must cover their workers' tax obligations.
He said the measure to be introduced in October would free 500 million dinars (about $100 million) that companies could use to boost production and working capital.
But experts said while the announced fiscal cut was a positive step, it would have an insignificant impact.
"It was high time the government decided to do something," Aleksandra Posarac of the Institute of Economic Sciences told Reuters. "It is just a drop in the ocean."

"The announced fiscal adjustment will clearly not have any significant impact on the economy," Posarac said. "The government should halve the taxes if it wants to radically ease the fiscal burden (on the economy)."
The Serbian parliament is expected to pass the tax law at its extraordinary session next Wednesday. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
